- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots the true peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below the immediate prior high.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting downward; apply a 1–3 day lag correction downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model overfits to recent trend; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
